programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Sionnach agus Maigheach (Fox & Hare)
programme.desc: Nuair a chluinneas Comhachag Sionnach a’ bruidhinn mu Mhaigheach mar a’ charaid as fheàrr a th’ aige, tha Comhachag ag iarraidh a’ cheart rud air a shon fhèin. Aon mhadainn, tha balùn dearg a’ nochdadh ri taobh na craoibhe aige. Seo a’ charaid as fheàrr aig Comhachag! Tha iad a’ dèanamh a h-uile rud còmhla gus an tòiseach am balùn ri searg. Tha Comhachag troimhe chèile. Ciamar idir a thogas Sionnach agus Maigheach a shunnd? When Fox mentions that Hare is his best friend, Owl decides that he needs a best friend, too. One morning, a red balloon suddenly appears near his tree. This is Owl’s new best friend! They do everything together, but then the balloon slowly starts to deflate. Owl is in despair. What can Fox and Hare do to cheer Owl up again?

programme.title: Beathaichean a’ Bocadaich
programme.desc: Tha Sophie a’ coimhead tron phrosbaig sheunta aice airson faicinn ciamar a bhios beathaichean a’ bocadaich. Tha i ag ionnsachadh mar a bhios diofar bheathaichean a’ gluasad agus cuide ri a caraidean, tha i a’ cruthachadh dannsa. An-diugh, danns coltach ri ailbhean agus feòrag! Sophie looks through her magic binoculars to find out how animals boogie. She learns how different animals dance and, along with her friends, creates a dance using animal movements. Join her and dance like an elephant and a squirrel!

programme.title: Meaban and Moo
programme.desc: Bidh Linda a’ tadhal air Meaban is Moo gus dùbhlain spòrsail a chur romhpa. Anns a’ phrògram seo tha i ag iarraidh orra trì rudan òir a lorg. Cha deach gu math dha Meaban a’ lorg òr a-muigh ach saoil am bi ionmhas ri lorg am measg an trealaich sa bhothan? Linda visits Meaban and Moo to set them fun challenges. In this programme, she tasks them with finding three gold items. Meaban has no luck finding gold outside, but perhaps there is treasure to be found amongst the junk in the hut?

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha Bèibidh Dràgon Brot’ mì-thoilichte oir chan fhaod e cluich leis an spàin bhrot’ oir tha ro mhòr dha. Gu fortanach, tha Beag a’ moladh gum faod e taic a thoirt dhaibh-san le bhith toirt am brot air ais dhan uamh – is abair g’eil e taiceil! Baby Soup Dragon is unhappy - he isn’t allowed to play with the soup spoon as it’s too big for him. Fortunately, Small suggests that he can help to deliver the soup instead - and he is hugely helpful!

programme.title: Na Clangairean
programme.desc: Tha bogsa dìomhaireachd air laighe air a’ phlanaid, le rudan annasach na bhroinn - clobhdan a tha nan tuill cuideachd. Tha e comasach dha na Clangairean siubhal tro na tuill seo - agus abair gu bheil iad trang a’ siubhal! A mysterious box has landed on the planet, with curious things inside it - cloths which are also holes. The Clangers can travel through these holes, and they do it a lot!

programme.title: Stòiridh
programme.desc: Sgeulachd do chlann òga. Tha Babs Nicgriogair a’ leughadh Eanraig agus an t-Inneal. Chaidh an leabhar a sgrìobhadh le Isabelle Marinov, a dhealbhachadh le Olga Shtonda agus chaidh eadar-theangachadh dhan Ghàidhlig le Morag Stiùbhart. A bedtime story for young children. Babs Macgregor reads Eanraig agus an t-Inneal, written by Isabelle Marinov, illustrated by Olga Shtonda and translated into Gaelic by Morag Stewart.

programme.title: Clann Na Cruinne
programme.desc: ‘S toigh le Valentin a bhith a’ farpais ri seòladairean eile. The e gu tur air a dhòigh air an uisge. ‘S e a mhiann coinneachadh ris a' churaidh, Armel le Cleac’h, seòladair a choisinn mòran dhuaisean aon-neach. Valentin loves to compete with other sailors and be on the water. His dream is to meet his hero, Armel le Cleac’h, a sailor who won a lot of solo trophies.

programme.title: Belle and Sebastian
programme.desc: Nuair a dh’iarr Ivan air Cameron agus Gabriel na caoraich a chur gu fuarach-samhraidh, tha Sebastian 'son aon rud a dhearbhadh - gur e Belle an cù-chaorach as fheàrr a th’ ann! When Cameron and Gabriel are responsible for moving Ivan’s sheep to summer pastures, Sebastian only has one goal, to prove that Belle is the best sheepdog around!

programme.title: Seonaidh | Shaun the Sheep
programme.desc: Tha an tuathanach a' faighinn tiodhlac neo-àbhaisteach bho co-ogha à Astràilia. Mì-thoilichte leis an tiodhlac, tha e a' feuchainn a thilgeil air falbh ach tha e gu daonnan a' tilleadh air ais, dha dhèanamh cinnteach gu bheil comas draoidheachd aig an rud. The Farmer receives a mystery gift from his antipodean cousin. However, he is unimpressed with the present and attempts to throw it away, only for it to keep reappearing. He becomes convinced it has magical powers.

programme.title: Uaine
programme.desc: Thòisich tramaichean a’ ruith ann an Dùn Èideann ann an 2014 agus an-diugh tha faisg air 20,000 duine gan chleachdadh gach latha. The Calum agus a cho-ogha Ruairidh Iain anns a’ bhaile airson barrachd innse dhuinn mun deidhinn. Trams started running in Edinburgh in 2014 and now nearly 20,000 people use them every day. Calum and his cousin Ruairidh Iain visit the city to tell us a bit more about them.

programme.title: Bogaisean is Gumbalan/Bottersnikes and Gumbles
programme.desc: Chan eil na Bògaisean neo na Gumbalan a’ faireachdainn gu math oir tha ’ad a’ fulang le biorgadh bodhaig. Feumar obrachadh le chèile airson leighis a lorg. Saoil am bi e comasach dhaibh seo a dhèanamh? The Bògaisean and the Gumbals are feeling unwell today as they’re suffering from boggle twitches. They must work together to find a cure. Will it be possible?

programme.title: Bus Ghlaschu/Glasgow Bus
programme.desc: Tha seinneadair Lorraine McIntosh à comhlan Deacon Blue eòlach air Bus Ghlaschu. Chi sinn Lorraine dol air ais a Dhùn nan Gall far a bheil ceangal teaghlaich aice. Lorraine MacIntosh, from Deacon Blue, knows the Glasgow bus well. Join the singer as she shares her connections to Donegal.

programme.title: SpeakGaelic
programme.desc: Claire Macleod from the Isle of Scalpay is Joy’s guest in the studio and Calum Maclean is on the hunt for some important pillars on the Isle of Skye.

programme.title: An Là
programme.desc: Naidheachdan ionadail, nàiseanta is eadar-nàiseanta gach là cuide ri fiosrachadh coimhearsnachd bho BBC ALBA. Local, national and international news and information from BBC ALBA.

programme.title: Immigration Tracks
programme.desc: From Canada's Eastern province of Cape Breton, we embark on a road-trip east to Toronto, Ontario in search of Scottish Gaelic families who settled in this vast country over 100 years ago. Anne picks up the chanter in the Canadian capital, Ottawa, and goes in search of a relative who once farmed cattle in Bolton, Ontario. How do generations of Canadian Scots identify with their roots? Join Anne McAlpine on a cultural voyage of discovery. An t-seachdains, bidh Anne a’ feuchainn ri port a chluich air an fheadan ann am prìomh bhaile Chanada, Ottawa. Bidh Anne cuideachd a’ dol gu Bolton, Ontario is ceangal-teaghlaich aice ri fear a bha uair a’ cumail chruidh san àite.

programme.title: Am Madadh-Allaidh
programme.desc: The history of the Scottish wolf and its extinction - is it time for their return? Eachdraidh a’mhadaidh-allaidh an Alba, bho chian a bith. A’ bheil an t-am aige tilleadh?

programme.title: Dàna | Scotland's Wild Side
programme.desc: Shetland’s expansive coastline is home to endless towering cliffs, but its remoteness from the mainland means they see few ascents. With a friend in tow, Coinneach Rankin travels to Shetland in search of new routes and spectacular climbing challenges. Tha oirthir fhada Shealtainn loma làn chreagan tomadach agus seallaidhean nach creidear, ach air sgàth cho cèin ’s a tha i bho thir-mòr, chan fhaigh cus an cothrom sreap ann. Le seann charaid na chuideachd, siubhailidh Coinneach MacFhraing a Shealtainn air tòir slighean ùra is dùbhlain bharraichte. In Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Leonardo da Vinci (BBC ALBA)
programme.desc: Ann am Florence, Milan, An Ròimh agus mu dheireadh an Fhraing, tha e a’ cur an t-eòlas saidheansail agus ealain an lùib aon de na dealbhan as cliùitiche anns an t-saoghal. In Florence, Milan, Rome and finally France, Leonardo pours the sum of his scientific and artistic knowledge into a portrait that would become the most famous painting ever. Dubbed in Gaelic with English subtitles.

programme.title: Port
programme.desc: Sreath aithriseach ciùil ùr ann an cuideachd Julie Fowlis agus Muireann NicAmhlaoibh, 's iad air slighe rannsachaidh mu na freumhan aca fhèin, a-nochd ann am Baile Àth-Cliath. Nì Port taisbeanadh air na ceanglaichean dualchais a tha eadar dithis a tha air a bhith na 'n caraidean 's na 'n companaich-ciùil fad iomadh bliadhna. Tha an seinneadair Darren MacIlleathain agus am pìobaire Carole-Ann NicAoidh a' tadhal air grunnd ionadan cliùiteach ann am Baile Àth-Cliath ann an cuideachd Julie is Muireann. Musical documentary with Julie Fowlis and Muireann NicAmhlaoibh as they take to the road to explore their shared musical roots. In Dublin, Port reveals their shared musical heritage. Port celebrates the common musical heritage of the longtime friends and collaborators as they cross borders and traditions between the west of Ireland and the Western Isles, meeting and playing with friends and musicians en route. Singer Darren MacLean and piper Carole-Anne MacKay join our musical hosts for a tour of several iconic venues. True to form, Dublin doesn't disappoint and gives up some musical gems.

programme.title: Seo BBC ALBA. This is BBC ALBA
programme.desc: Sealladh ùr bho Alba. A new view from Scotland.

programme.title: Genius of the Ancient World
programme.desc: In the final episode, Bettany travels to China on the trail of Confucius, a great sage of Chinese history whose ideas have fundamentally shaped the country of his birth for around 2,500 years.

programme.title: Lost Cities of the Ancients
programme.desc: In the Lambeyeque valley in northern Peru lies a strange lost world - the forgotten ruins of 250 mysterious pyramids, including some of the biggest on the planet, colossal structures made out of mud bricks. Long ago, the Lambeyeque people were haunted by a terrible fear and believed that building pyramids was essential to their survival. Their obsession reached its height at a city called Tucume, an eerie place of 26 pyramids standing side by side, the last pyramids this civilisation created before they vanished forever. What was the fear that drove these people to build so many pyramids, what were they for and why did the whole civilisation suddenly vanish? This film captures the moments when archaeologists at the site uncovered a mass of bodies of human sacrifice victims, following a trail of clues into the dark story of Tucume. It recreates the strange rituals of the people of the valley, revealing a civilisation whose obsession to build pyramids eventually turned to horror, until Tucume finally vanished in a bloody frenzy of human sacrifice.

programme.title: Only Connect
programme.desc: Quiz show presented by Victoria Coren in which knowledge will only take you so far, as patience and lateral thinking are also vital. It is all about making connections between things which may appear, at first glance, not to be connected at all.

programme.title: Inside Porton Down: Britain's Secret Weapons Research Facility
programme.desc: Dr Michael Mosley investigates Britain's most secretive and controversial military research base, Porton Down, on its 100th anniversary. He comes face to face with chemical and biological weapons old and new, reveals the truth about shocking animal and human testing, and discovers how the latest science and technology are helping to defend us against terrorist attacks and rogue nations.

programme.title: The Ruth Ellis Files: A Very British Crime Story
programme.desc: Series re-examining the Ruth Ellis case. Gillian Pachter takes a forensic look at the police investigation and discovers worrying assumptions and problematic omissions.

programme.title: Remembers...
programme.desc: Acclaimed screenwriter Stephen Poliakoff shares his memories of the BBC's 1980 television drama Caught on a Train, his Bafta award-winning collaboration with celebrated producer Kenith Trodd. The drama was based on a real-life encounter Stephen experienced with an angry fellow passenger on a train trip across Europe. It stars the legendary Dame Peggy Ashcroft and Michael Kitchen as strangers who clash at the start of their journey but come to an understanding by the time they reach their destination. Here, Stephen reveals how the production came together, why he was left thinking the drama may herald the end of his career, and which iconic James Bond villainess was almost cast as the leading lady.

programme.title: Playhouse
programme.desc: A young Englishman, travelling on the Ostend to Vienna express, shares a train compartment with an American girl and an elderly Viennese lady.

programme.title: How to Get Ahead
programme.desc: Writer, broadcaster and Newsnight arts correspondent Stephen Smith explores Renaissance Florence under the reign of Grand Duke Cosimo Medici. Cosimo's fledgling court prized the finer things in life and some of the greatest painters, sculptors and craftsmen in world history came to serve the Grand Duke. But successful courtiers had to have brains as well as brawn. The canniest of them looked to theorists like Niccolo Machiavelli for underhand ways to get ahead, whilst enlightened polymaths turned their minds to the heavens, and to ice cream.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The devoted owners of no fewer than six Irish wolfhounds are in desperate need of more space for them and those countless muddy paws, so have set their sights on Suffolk for a bit more elbow room. Briony May Williams is there to guide them as they tour a selection of beautiful homes. Briony also gets to mess about on a stunning million pound, bespoke wooden yacht, a sister vessel to the ones featured in James Bond.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the high-stakes quiz, joined by a celebrity team featuring comedian and actor Phil Wang, dating expert Anna Williamson, actor and comedian Miles Jupp and actor Jamie-Lee O’Donnell as they take on the Bridge of Lies in support of their chosen charities. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Breakfast
programme.desc: The latest news, sport, business and weather from the BBC's Breakfast team.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The devoted owners of no fewer than six Irish wolfhounds are in desperate need of more space for them and those countless muddy paws, so have set their sights on Suffolk for a bit more elbow room. Briony May Williams is there to guide them as they tour a selection of beautiful homes. Briony also gets to mess about on a stunning million pound, bespoke wooden yacht, a sister vessel to the ones featured in James Bond.

Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The devoted owners of no fewer than six Irish wolfhounds are in desperate need of more space for them and those countless muddy paws, so have set their sights on Suffolk for a bit more elbow room. programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The devoted owners of no fewer than six Irish wolfhounds are in desperate need of more space for them and those countless muddy paws, so have set their sights on Suffolk for a bit more elbow room. Briony May Williams is there to guide them as they tour a selection of beautiful homes. Briony also gets to mess about on a stunning million pound, bespoke wooden yacht, a sister vessel to the ones featured in James Bond.

programme.title: Bridge of Lies
programme.desc: Ross Kemp presents the quiz show where a team of four – in this episode, friends Jordan, Allan, Archie and Lewis – take on the Bridge of Lies. One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Pointless
programme.desc: Alexander Armstrong is joined by co-host Angela Scanlon for the brainy quiz where the contestants try to score as few points as possible by plumbing the depths of their general knowledge to come up with the answers no-one else could think of.

One by one, they all face the Bridge, choosing who faces each crossing depending on the question category. Each Bridge crossing has 32 potential steps, including 22 truths and ten lies. They must cross the Bridge by stepping on the truths and avoiding the lies, earning money for each correct answer. Step on a lie and the Bridge will halve their money. Step on three lies, and they are out of the game. There is always a safe path across the Bridge. They just have to find it. Once they have each faced the Bridge on their own, those who have been successful will join forces to face the final crossing for a chance to take home the cash.

programme.title: Morning Live
programme.desc: Join Gethin Jones, Helen Skelton, Michelle Ackerley and the team for conversation, advice and tips to make your day that little bit easier.

programme.title: Rip Off Britain
programme.desc: How much can you trust your MOT? In a special scams episode, Gloria Hunniford, Julia Somerville and Louise Minchin investigate the so-called ‘ghost’ MOTs available for sale – and hear from the mum whose second-hand car was far from roadworthy. The team reveal what happened when they tried to buy fake MOTs online. And the advice clinic heads to Reading to help the man who paid more than £200 for gift cards as Christmas presents for his family but discovered most of them had already been redeemed. The team’s research reveals which gift cards are most susceptible to being spent by scammers before customers have had a chance to use them.

programme.title: Homes Under the Hammer
programme.desc: Martin is in London to meet a mum helping her daughter to get on the property ladder. Jacqui’s perplexed by the layout of two linked flats that she feels should just be one. And Tommy feels like he’s in a Swedish sauna, given the amount of timber inside a Staffordshire terrace.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Students take on lecturers in a battle of the brains! In red are friends Amy and Laura, who study history and maths – which they hope will be an ideal combination for bargain hunting! Their opponents in blue are Karen and Nick, who plan to ‘teach the reds a lesson’. With pride at stake, both teams dash around an antiques fair in Wetherby in search of three profitable items to sell at auction. Guiding the reds is Philip Serrell, who reckons he’s as old as some of the items his team are looking at! Maths undergraduate Laura isn’t impressed with a calculating machine, and the team turn up their noses at a perfume atomiser. Giving the blues an education in antiques is Jonathan Pratt. A rusty vintage biscuit tin gives them food for thought, but they decide a model of a Red Arrows jet won’t fly in the saleroom. While the teams shop, presenter Caroline Hawley is on home turf in Yorkshire as she quizzes fair-goers about a horsehair-stuffed mystery item! Over in Ripon, will it be 'neigh' or 'yay' from the bidders when the teams’ items go under the hammer?

programme.title: BBC News at One
programme.desc: The latest national and international news from the BBC.

programme.title: Scam Interceptors
programme.desc: The team track a tech support scammer working out of New Delhi as he tries to steal money from a man in the UK. As the scammer remotely accesses the man’s computer, the team try desperately to get him on the phone and explain that his money is at serious risk. The man lives in a park home, which gives the team an opportunity. Can they convince the park’s employees to help? Also on the programme, we chat to a scammer posing as Jennifer Aniston.

programme.title: Attenborough and the Sea Dragon
programme.desc: A remarkable 200-million-year-old fossil - the bones of an ichthyosaur, a giant sea dragon - has been discovered on the Jurassic coast of Britain. David Attenborough joins the hunt to bring this ancient creature's story to life. Using state-of-the-art imaging technology and CGI, the team reconstruct the skeleton and create the most detailed animation of an ichthyosaur ever made. Along the way, the team stumble into a 200-million-year-old murder mystery. Only painstaking forensic investigation can unravel the story of this extraordinary creature's fate.

programme.title: Escape to the Country
programme.desc: The devoted owners of no fewer than six Irish wolfhounds are in desperate need of more space for them and those countless muddy paws, so have set their sights on Suffolk for a bit more elbow room. Briony May Williams is there to guide them as they tour a selection of beautiful homes. Briony also gets to mess about on a stunning million pound, bespoke wooden yacht, a sister vessel to the ones featured in James Bond.

programme.title: Scotland's Home of the Year
programme.desc: In the south, the judges must choose between an extended family home near Gatehouse of Fleet, a quirky cottage in Isle of Whithorn or a scenic refurbished home in Thornhill. programme.title: This Farming Life
programme.desc: Emma suspects the pond is being visited by more than their local fishermen after secret cameras reveal a variety of hungry callers. The Williamsons take their ram lambs to a prestigious sale on the mainland, hoping to make big money and secure their reputation as top tup breeders. Lucy and Lottie enter the young handlers competition at the Arran Show.

programme.title: Sally Magnusson: Alzheimer's, a Cure and Me
programme.desc: Sally Magnusson and her family cared for their mother for many years before her death from dementia. With a possible familial link, Sally has often wondered: Will I be next? Now a cure for Alzheimer’s is in sight – but the scientists need people like Sally to be tested. She can find out if she has the invisible indications of Alzheimer’s in her brain already by being part of a groundbreaking study of 'healthy brains' at Scotland’s pioneering brain clinic. With privileged access to Sally’s sisters, her own children and their extensive family archive, this film paints a portrait of a family as they weigh up a potentially life-changing decision.

programme.title: Scotland's Greatest Escape
programme.desc: Judith Ralston and Grado sample Scotland’s south coast in Dumfries and Galloway. They experience majestic birds of prey on the Galloway Red Kite Trail, and spend the night in coastal glamping domes. Their final stop takes them to Portpatrick, where they stay in the Edwardian luxury of Dunskey Castle.

programme.title: The Green Planet
programme.desc: More kinds of plants are crammed together in the tropical rainforests than anywhere else on Earth. The result is astonishing beauty and intense competition - a plant battleground. New filming techniques allow us to enter the plants’ world and see it from their perspective and on their timescale. From fast-growing trees to flowers that mimic dead animals, this is a journey into a magical world that operates on a different timescale to our own.

programme.title: See Hear
programme.desc: A look at love and relationships in the deaf community, from a couple married for over 50 years to honest conversations about modern dating and finding connection today. Presenter Rolf Choutan is joined by award-winning photographer Becky Bailey, whose work capturing weddings has given her a unique window into the many forms that love can take. Together, they discuss relationships, communication and how connection evolves over time.

programme.title: Twenty Twenty Six
programme.desc: Sarah’s slip of the tongue on Alicia Byrd’s podcast means that she’s now gone viral as the ‘wooden condoms girl’. The oversight team decide it would be a good idea if she does a live interview on one of the many network news shows clamouring to meet her. But although Sarah agrees, she’s completely unprepared for the idea of millions of people watching her. Around the same time, rumours break on social media about a high-profile footballer, resulting in the team needing to draw up an official statement which everyone can agree on.

programme.title: Inside Barlinnie
programme.desc: Long-term addict Bobby heads to rehab, Billy fights for recognition that he has really changed, while Alan is released and heads back to his old ways on Glasgow's streets.

programme.title: This is BBC Two
programme.desc: Highlights of programmes on BBC Two.

programme.title: Bargain Hunt
programme.desc: Christina Trevanion buckles up in a vintage American muscle car to take a spin around one of Britain’s fastest racetracks. At 1.85 miles long, Castle Combe in Wiltshire is a popular circuit for vintage racing cars and has hosted some of the world’s motor racing greats. Christina rides shotgun with noise-monitoring officer Dave Hensley to learn about the history of the track and why drivers need to have their wits about them as they navigate its hair-raising straights and bends. Motoring around an antiques fair in Devon are two teams of families. In red are dad and daughter Alan and Maisie, guided by antiques expert Ben Cooper. Their opponents in blue are mum and daughter Denise and Amy, with expert Gary Pe. Alan kicks off the reds’ shop by picking out a contemporary glass vase, but Ben doesn’t see a profit in it. Meanwhile, a pair of miniature wooden doll's chairs catch Denise’s eye, but does Gary think they’ll bring a big return? programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael begins his journey at the Demilitarised Zone, the heavily fortified border that has divided the Korean peninsula since the end of the Korean War. From the DMZ, Michael travels south by rail into Seoul, arriving in a vast, fast-moving capital that has risen from the ruins of war to become one of the world’s most advanced cities. Exploring palaces and the restored Cheonggyecheon stream, he uncovers how tradition and innovation coexist in everyday Korean life. Michael’s first Korean leg ends at Kukkiwon, the World Taekwondo Headquarters, where he discovers how Korea’s national martial art reflects discipline, resilience and a hard-won modern identity.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Leaving Seoul aboard South Korea’s high-speed KTX train, Michael travels south through the heart of the country to explore how rail has shaped both its economy and identity. His first stop is Daejeon, a centre of science and education, where a local bakery founded by a North Korean refugee offers a small but telling story of postwar resilience. Nearby, in Geumsan, Michael visits a ginseng research institute to discover how Korea’s most prized root, cultivated for over 1,500 years, has evolved from traditional medicine into a global health and skincare industry. Continuing east along the historic Gyeongbu line, Michael learns how Korea’s railways, first laid at the end of the 19th century, became the backbone of the modern nation. In Gyeongju, the ancient capital of the Silla dynasty, he joins archaeologists excavating royal burial mounds, uncovering gold artefacts that reveal the story of Korea’s first unification. The journey ends in Busan, where Michael explores a hillside community built by war refugees and meets an artist whose work reflects the city’s enduring legacy of displacement, creativity and renewal.

While the Peelers wait for CCTV footage to come in, the suspect tells Stephen about his prolific criminal past, his hatred of police and struggles with addiction.

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Michael begins his journey at the Demilitarised Zone, the heavily fortified border that has divided the Korean peninsula since the end of the Korean War. From the track of a long-abandoned railway near the Imjin River, he explores one of the most tense frontiers in the world and reflects on a conflict that ended in ceasefire but never peace. From the DMZ, Michael travels south by rail into Seoul, arriving in a vast, fast-moving capital that has risen from the ruins of war to become one of the world’s most advanced cities. Exploring palaces and the restored Cheonggyecheon stream, he uncovers how tradition and innovation coexist in everyday Korean life. At the BBC’s Seoul bureau, Michael meets the news editor broadcasting news into North Korea, before sharing street food with a North Korean defector who poignantly describes the personal cost of division. Michael’s first Korean leg ends at Kukkiwon, the World Taekwondo Headquarters, where he discovers how Korea’s national martial art reflects discipline, resilience and a hard-won modern identity.

programme.title: Greatest Gardens with Diarmuid Gavin and Carol Klein

Diarmuid, Carol and Prue are searching for a garden which the owners have poured their heart and soul into creating. Which will they decide deserves a place in the final?

programme.title: Clean It, Fix It
programme.desc: The team visit south Wales, coming to the rescue of a busy entrepreneur who has no time to fix her house. They must organise her messy living room into a space that the whole family can use and where she can run her business effectively, whilst also cleaning and organising months of clutter and grime.

programme.title: Big Cats 24/7
programme.desc: The team continue following the Okavango Delta’s lions, leopards and cheetahs. After a huge wildfire, Gordon Buchanan and Vianet Djenguet trail the lion pride’s dominant males, Big Toe and Madumo, as they reinstate their burnt-out boundaries and fight with intruder males. Brad Bestelink follows Xudum the leopardess as she learns to hunt from trees after the fire wipes out her cover. And Anna Dimitriadis sticks with hungry resident cheetah Pobe day and night as she tries to hunt.

programme.title: Antiques Roadshow
programme.desc: Michael Aspel and a team of experts invite members of the public to bring along their antiques for examination. In Stroud, Gloucestershire, they find a strange 17th-century cushion mirror and an early marine chronometer that might be worth fifty thousand pounds. Meanwhile, Michael finds a Borneo headhunter's sword.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This edition comes from Dover Castle in Kent, where antiques experts James Lewis and Catherine Southon search for items to take off to auction. James unearths a silver owl inkwell, and Catherine discovers an alabaster bust. Paul Martin delves into the history of the English Channel.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Leaving Seoul aboard South Korea’s high-speed KTX train, Michael travels south through the heart of the country to explore how rail has shaped both its economy and identity. His first stop is Daejeon, a centre of science and education, where a local bakery founded by a North Korean refugee offers a small but telling story of postwar resilience. Nearby, in Geumsan, Michael visits a ginseng research institute to discover how Korea’s most prized root, cultivated for over 1,500 years, has evolved from traditional medicine into a global health and skincare industry. Continuing east along the historic Gyeongbu line, Michael learns how Korea’s railways, first laid at the end of the 19th century, became the backbone of the modern nation. In Gyeongju, the ancient capital of the Silla dynasty, he joins archaeologists excavating royal burial mounds, uncovering gold artefacts that reveal the story of Korea’s first unification. The journey ends in Busan, where Michael explores a hillside community built by war refugees and meets an artist whose work reflects the city’s enduring legacy of displacement, creativity and renewal.

programme.title: Iolo's River Valleys
programme.desc: Iolo Williams explores the Usk valley, from Newport’s urban wildlife to ground-nesting birds, a huge lesser horseshoe bat roost and scarce firecrests.

programme.title: Blue Planet II
programme.desc: This extended special of the nature documentary series journeys from the equator to the unexplored depths, meeting the best-loved characters from the series.

programme.title: Surgeons: At the Edge of Life
programme.desc: One patient’s rare penis cancer requires a partial amputation, and another patient with severe endometriosis must have a huge cyst and a damaged kidney removed.

programme.title: Peelers: The PSNI for Real
programme.desc: On patrol in the city centre, Adam and Nigel receive reports of men fleeing police. As they round the corner, they spot them legging it. Adam takes pursuit, tackles and detains one of the suspects. A few minutes later, unbelievably, he must do it again, as the man bursts out of the police car, trying to escape. Back at the station, Anna and Perri can’t resist the temptation to hide the boss’s car, temporarily. Meanwhile, the whole team leap into action when a stolen car fails to stop for Adam. When the driver runs off, Dave relies on his years of experience and pays a visit to a serial car thief matching the driver’s description. While the Peelers wait for CCTV footage to come in, the suspect tells Stephen about his prolific criminal past, his hatred of police and struggles with addiction.

Meanwhile, Michael finds a Borneo headhunter's sword.

programme.title: Flog It!
programme.desc: This edition comes from Dover Castle in Kent, where antiques experts James Lewis and Catherine Southon search for items to take off to auction. James unearths a silver owl inkwell, and Catherine discovers an alabaster bust. Paul Martin delves into the history of the English Channel.

programme.title: Richard Osman's House of Games
programme.desc: Every day this week, celebrity contestants Jordan Banjo, Sian Lloyd, Nick Pickard and Ellie White take on a series of quiz rounds selected by the host, quiz legend Richard Osman. A daily winner is declared following a quickfire round at the end of each show, and the scores are tallied across the week, resulting in an overall champion being crowned on Friday. Will the winning stars opt for the much-coveted House of Games wheelie luggage, or will they be tempted with the very popular bee hotel?

programme.title: Great Korean Railway Journeys
programme.desc: Leaving Seoul aboard South Korea’s high-speed KTX train, Michael travels south through the heart of the country to explore how rail has shaped both its economy and identity. His first stop is Daejeon, a centre of science and education, where a local bakery founded by a North Korean refugee offers a small but telling story of postwar resilience. Nearby, in Geumsan, Michael visits a ginseng research institute to discover how Korea’s most prized root, cultivated for over 1,500 years, has evolved from traditional medicine into a global health and skincare industry. Continuing east along the historic Gyeongbu line, Michael learns how Korea’s railways, first laid at the end of the 19th century, became the backbone of the modern nation. In Gyeongju, the ancient capital of the Silla dynasty, he joins archaeologists excavating royal burial mounds, uncovering gold artefacts that reveal the story of Korea’s first unification. The journey ends in Busan, where Michael explores a hillside community built by war refugees and meets an artist whose work reflects the city’s enduring legacy of displacement, creativity and renewal.

programme.title: This Is a Bomb: The Nevada Casino Heist

programme.title: One Zoo Three
programme.desc: The One Zoo Three brothers explore San Diego Zoo Safari Park in the US and come face to face with rhinos, giraffes and the California condor. Tyler is faced with one of the biggest piles of poo he he has ever seen while on the trail of a crash of white rhinos. But this is no ordinary mountain of muck – Tyler discovers the importance of a rhino loo and what these animals can do with a pile of poo! Meanwhile, Aaron is lucky enough to go behind the scenes at the safari park’s special lab, where he discovers how the latest science is being used to bring back certain species, such as the beautiful Przewalski’s horse, from the brink of extinction, . Cam has a unique opportunity to look at a California condor chick inside an egg and to hand-feed a young lappet-faced vulture, with the help of an unusual puppet. Cute Alert introduces an adorable little beauty who lives up high in the branches – Som, the Matschie’s tree-kangaroo. And Aaron sticks his neck out to reveal some real wows and wonders about the giraffe –- but are they fact or fake?

Luckily, a bulrush can BEND to make a bridge for the little bug to cross and arrive before the others.

programme.title: Peter Rabbit

programme.title: Hey Duggee

programme.desc: Juno’s best friend is a baby bird and they talk all day, but when anyone else talks to him, he freezes up. Vida figures out the problem—he’s shy—and gives the baby bird some tools to help him cope.

programme.title: Supertato

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: While waiting to be picked up from school, Jack plays at being a sailor lost at sea.

programme.title: Piripenguins

programme.title: Bluey

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: With the harbour master away, Penny Pocket tends to his beloved pet plant, Colin. But Colin is in a sad and droopy state - she needs to find a way to get him better!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is unwell. He's in his pyjamas and under strict orders to stay in bed and rest. But poor Waffle can't get comfy. When he sees Evie and Simon playing in the garden, he feels left out and begins to woof and woof. Simon tells Waffle to rest quietly, but it's too late. The wonder dog's incessant barking has already disturbed Mrs Hobbs next door and, to make matters worse, like Waffle she's not feeling well either. Mrs Hobbs has a bad cold, and she's blaming it on the Brooklyn-Bells. She's convinced getting drenched in their ball-pit pond is the cause. The Brooklyn-Bells do chores for Mrs Hobbs to help her get better, and Jess brings home a surprise from work.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard

At first, it’s funny - they eat, play and do homework side by side. But soon their different ideas cause squabbles. With help from Jake and Dash, they remember why they wanted to stay together in the first place. Even best friends have differences, and that’s what makes them special.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran miss their bus home, so the pair settle down to wait for the next one. But getting the bus isn’t quite as simple as JoJo thinks it is. A wrong bus later and the pair are back where they started! It’s time to look at the schedule and see when their bus is due to arrive.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: The Iron Chicken is in her nest singing along to her radio, when suddenly it stops working. Major Clanger is fishing nearby and tries to repair it on the spot but in the end decides he will have to take it to his workshop. The Iron Chicken is distraught but Granny assures her that Major knows what he’s doing, and reluctantly the Iron Chicken returns to her nest where she receives a visit from the Wols, who suggest they create their own radio station – Radio Wol. It is a huge success.

programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read stories. Everybody is running about in the garden so much that Makka Pakka can't wash faces. After a lot of fun and chasing, they all come together and Makka Pakka succeeds in his task.

programme.title: Teletubbies

programme.desc: Nori and Dot are stuck in a treehouse without a door. How can Mojo and Bo get them out? By sending the treehouse flying across town, that’s how!

programme.desc: After Old Brown snatches her, Cotton-tail gets stuck up a tree. It's up to Peter, Lily and Benjamin to rescue her before either a passing Mr Tod seizes her or the angry owl returns.

programme.title: Hey Duggee
programme.desc: The Squirrels go out for a walk but can't find a way back to the clubhouse. Through a series of unusual methods, the Squirrels learn all about direction and how to find their way to the clubhouse.

programme.title: Vida the Vet
programme.desc: Juno’s best friend is a baby bird and they talk all day, but when anyone else talks to him, he freezes up. Vida figures out the problem—he’s shy—and gives the baby bird some tools to help him cope.

programme.title: Supertato
programme.desc: Evil Pea takes over the Tato Tower HQ and uses Carrot’s new security system to keep Supertato out. Supertato and Carrot work on a cunning ice cream plan to sneak back in.

programme.title: The Weasy Family
programme.desc: The ducklings want a pet, but Weasy isn't keen on changing his comfortable life. He finally gives in and lets them adopt a crab, but it soon starts wreaking havoc in the hayloft. Weasy has to do something about it.

programme.title: Mojo Swoptops
programme.desc: There’s a girder out of place on Swoppiton Bridge, and unless Nori can fix it, that bridge is coming down! Luckily, Mojo’s got the tops, and Bo’s got the skills to help get it done.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: While waiting to be picked up from school, Jack plays at being a sailor lost at sea.

programme.title: Piripenguins
programme.desc: After a spate of unfortunate accidents, Pancake is convinced that rubbing a lucky icicle will bring him good luck but panics when it’s rubbed away, until his friends step in.

programme.title: Bluey
programme.desc: Mum bans the girls from saying 'dunny', so they try and trick her into saying it instead.

programme.title: Balamory
programme.desc: With the harbour master away, Penny Pocket tends to his beloved pet plant, Colin. But Colin is in a sad and droopy state - she needs to find a way to get him better!

programme.title: Waffle the Wonder Dog
programme.desc: Waffle is unwell. He's in his pyjamas and under strict orders to stay in bed and rest. But poor Waffle can't get comfy. When he sees Evie and Simon playing in the garden, he feels left out and begins to woof and woof. Simon tells Waffle to rest quietly, but it's too late. The wonder dog's incessant barking has already disturbed Mrs Hobbs next door and, to make matters worse, like Waffle she's not feeling well either. Mrs Hobbs has a bad cold, and she's blaming it on the Brooklyn-Bells. She's convinced getting drenched in their ball-pit pond is the cause. The Brooklyn-Bells do chores for Mrs Hobbs to help her get better, and Jess brings home a surprise from work.

programme.title: Rafi the Wishing Wizard
programme.desc: Rafi and Ruby are having the best play date ever, and they don't want Ruby to go home, so they make a wish to be stuck together. At first, it’s funny - they eat, play and do homework side by side. But soon their different ideas cause squabbles. With help from Jake and Dash, they remember why they wanted to stay together in the first place. Even best friends have differences, and that’s what makes them special.

programme.title: JoJo & Gran Gran
programme.desc: JoJo and Gran Gran miss their bus home, so the pair settle down to wait for the next one. But getting the bus isn’t quite as simple as JoJo thinks it is. A wrong bus later and the pair are back where they started! It’s time to look at the schedule and see when their bus is due to arrive.

programme.title: Sarah & Duck
programme.desc: Animation. Sarah and her best friend Duck embark on simple but exciting adventures, exploring the world both near and far in their own wobbly and imaginative way. Sarah's brand new bouncy ball has a rather unexpected problem.

programme.title: Clangers
programme.desc: The Iron Chicken is in her nest singing along to her radio, when suddenly it stops working. Major Clanger is fishing nearby and tries to repair it on the spot but in the end decides he will have to take it to his workshop. The Iron Chicken is distraught but Granny assures her that Major knows what he’s doing, and reluctantly the Iron Chicken returns to her nest where she receives a visit from the Wols, who suggest they create their own radio station – Radio Wol. It is a huge success.

programme.title: BeddyByes
programme.desc: MeMo and BaBa pretend to be racing cars. At Play Time, they choose a ride-on car to play with. BaBa loves the feeling of being pushed along, while MeMo loves to make the wheels spin. MeMo and BaBa push Yummy Dog in the Yummy cart, making the wheels go round before enjoying some wheel-shaped pasta. On the Lullaby Lake, Fungi and Pungi perform cartwheels as MeMo and BaBa make their way to Gramma Leeba.

programme.title: In the Night Garden
programme.desc: In a magical forest, colourful characters have adventures and are read stories. Everybody is running about in the garden so much that Makka Pakka can't wash faces. After a lot of fun and chasing, they all come together and Makka Pakka succeeds in his task.

programme.title: WhatsApp Obsession: The Murder of Stephanie Hansen
programme.desc: On the 30th of December, 2022, 39-year-old Stephanie Hansen was brutally stabbed to death in her London home - her housemate and friend Sheldon Rodrigues initially appeared grief-stricken, yet behind his facade lay a chilling obsession. In the months before Stephanie's death, Rodrigues planted secret cameras and recording devices in their home and bombarded her with coercive WhatsApp messages - when Steph began a new relationship, his jealousy turned deadly. Through exclusive access to police bodycam footage, WhatsApp records and court evidence, this film reveals how the Metropolitan Police exposed Rodrigues' lies and uncovered the disturbing level of surveillance Steph was subjected to - featuring interviews with Steph's family, friends and the detectives who investigated the case, this powerful documentary unravels a story of obsession, control, and the ultimate betrayal.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Nicola Sturgeon faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Why did she separate from her husband? Who does she like least in politics? From her arrest to her love life, nothing is off limits as The Assembly get straight to the heart of a former leader - now unleashed. As the questions come thick and fast, Sturgeon opens up about grief, guilt and the loss of her baby, reflects on her complicated relationship with her former mentor Alex Salmond, and reveals what she'd say to her younger self. Along the way, there's talk of wine, Buckfast, Sean Connery, and whether she's due a new hairstyle. From the deeply personal to the downright cheeky, this is Nicola Sturgeon as you've never seen her before. Expect honesty, emotion, laughter - and a few moments that take everyone by surprise.

programme.title: WhatsApp Obsession: The Murder of Stephanie Hansen
programme.desc: On the 30th of December, 2022, 39-year-old Stephanie Hansen was brutally stabbed to death in her London home - her housemate and friend Sheldon Rodrigues initially appeared grief-stricken, yet behind his facade lay a chilling obsession. In the months before Stephanie's death, Rodrigues planted secret cameras and recording devices in their home and bombarded her with coercive WhatsApp messages - when Steph began a new relationship, his jealousy turned deadly. Through exclusive access to police bodycam footage, WhatsApp records and court evidence, this film reveals how the Metropolitan Police exposed Rodrigues' lies and uncovered the disturbing level of surveillance Steph was subjected to - featuring interviews with Steph's family, friends and the detectives who investigated the case, this powerful documentary unravels a story of obsession, control, and the ultimate betrayal.

Who does she like least in politics? From her arrest to her love life, nothing is off limits as The Assembly get straight to the heart of a former leader - now unleashed. As the questions come thick and fast, Sturgeon opens up about grief, guilt and the loss of her baby, reflects on her complicated relationship with her former mentor Alex Salmond, and reveals what she'd say to her younger self. Along the way, there's talk of wine, Buckfast, Sean Connery, and whether she's due a new hairstyle. From the deeply personal to the downright cheeky, this is Nicola Sturgeon as you've never seen her before. Expect honesty, emotion, laughter - and a few moments that take everyone by surprise.

programme.title: WhatsApp Obsession: The Murder of Stephanie Hansen
programme.desc: On the 30th of December, 2022, 39-year-old Stephanie Hansen was brutally stabbed to death in her London home - her housemate and friend Sheldon Rodrigues initially appeared grief-stricken, yet behind his facade lay a chilling obsession. In the months before Stephanie's death, Rodrigues planted secret cameras and recording devices in their home and bombarded her with coercive WhatsApp messages - when Steph began a new relationship, his jealousy turned deadly. Through exclusive access to police bodycam footage, WhatsApp records and court evidence, this film reveals how the Metropolitan Police exposed Rodrigues' lies and uncovered the disturbing level of surveillance Steph was subjected to - featuring interviews with Steph's family, friends and the detectives who investigated the case, this powerful documentary unravels a story of obsession, control, and the ultimate betrayal.

programme.desc: On the 30th of December, 2022, 39-year-old Stephanie Hansen was brutally stabbed to death in her London home - her housemate and friend Sheldon Rodrigues initially appeared grief-stricken, yet behind his facade lay a chilling obsession. In the months before Stephanie's death, Rodrigues planted secret cameras and recording devices in their home and bombarded her with coercive WhatsApp messages - when Steph began a new relationship, his jealousy turned deadly. Through exclusive access to police bodycam footage, WhatsApp records and court evidence, this film reveals how the Metropolitan Police exposed Rodrigues' lies and uncovered the disturbing level of surveillance Steph was subjected to - featuring interviews with Steph's family, friends and the detectives who investigated the case, this powerful documentary unravels a story of obsession, control, and the ultimate betrayal.

programme.title: The Assembly
programme.desc: Nicola Sturgeon faces the grilling of a lifetime from a cast of autistic and learning-disabled interviewers. Why did she separate from her husband? Who does she like least in politics? From her arrest to her love life, nothing is off limits as The Assembly get straight to the heart of a former leader - now unleashed. As the questions come thick and fast, Sturgeon opens up about grief, guilt and the loss of her baby, reflects on her complicated relationship with her former mentor Alex Salmond, and reveals what she'd say to her younger self. Along the way, there's talk of wine, Buckfast, Sean Connery, and whether she's due a new hairstyle. From the deeply personal to the downright cheeky, this is Nicola Sturgeon as you've never seen her before. Expect honesty, emotion, laughter - and a few moments that take everyone by surprise.

programme.title: WhatsApp Obsession: The Murder of Stephanie Hansen
programme.desc: On the 30th of December, 2022, 39-year-old Stephanie Hansen was brutally stabbed to death in her London home - her housemate and friend Sheldon Rodrigues initially appeared grief-stricken, yet behind his facade lay a chilling obsession. In the months before Stephanie's death, Rodrigues planted secret cameras and recording devices in their home and bombarded her with coercive WhatsApp messages - when Steph began a new relationship, his jealousy turned deadly. Through exclusive access to police bodycam footage, WhatsApp records and court evidence, this film reveals how the Metropolitan Police exposed Rodrigues' lies and uncovered the disturbing level of surveillance Steph was subjected to - featuring interviews with Steph's family, friends and the detectives who investigated the case, this powerful documentary unravels a story of obsession, control, and the ultimate betrayal.

programme.title: G'wed
programme.desc: Comedy series providing an honest, uplifting and heart-warming portrayal of the lives of working-class teenagers from Liverpool while tackling issues with a refreshing humour. It's Diversity and Inclusion Week and The Brimble, the most 'woke' girl at the school, has convinced the headmaster that the pupils should be set the task of pairing up with their polar opposite and present their differences and common ground in a presentation. Mo, who has fancied The Brimble for ages, spots his opportunity to try and impress her by suggesting they team up as he is a devout practising Muslim (he's not). Fascinated by his alleged faith, The Brimble leaps at the chance and asks if she can come to his house to observe a real Muslim family - keen to keep up the pretence, Mo calls his non-practicing Muslim parents and begs them to help him out. They agree... but when Mo and The Brimble arrive at the house, it becomes apparent that they are going to teach their son a life lesson about truth and faith.

programme.title: Olivia & Alex: Parenthood
programme.desc: Love Island’s Olivia & Alex Bowen invite us behind the scenes of family life as they juggle careers and parenting, while struggling to find quality time together as a couple. After early scans raised the excitement of expecting twins, the episode begins with an emotional appearance on Loose Women, where they describe their experience of Vanishing Twin Syndrome. As the birth of their daughter grows closer, Olivia feels the strain of daily life, while Alex’s decision to enter a bodybuilding competition couldn’t come at a busier time. Their 3-year-old son Abel provides endless laughs and challenges, from chaotic early mornings, to heart-melting moments at his swimming lessons. Through all the ups and downs, Olivia and Alex’s playful banter shines, especially when Alex’s carelessness threatens to derail their romantic Paris getaway. Honest, warm and full of heart, this is not just reality TV — it’s a candid, funny and deeply relatable look at love, loss and modern family life.

programme.title: Hell's Kitchen
programme.desc: The American version of Gordon Ramsay's culinary boot camp. The competition turns deeply personal as Chef Ramsay surprises the final three with emotional visits from their families at Foxwoods Resort and Casino - with the finale fast approaching, the remaining chefs get one last boost of love and pressure before everything is put on the line. After being treated to a glamorous day of hair, make-up and styling, the final three are thrown straight into one of the series' most high-stakes challenges yet. A panel of celebrity judges takes control of their fate, tasting dishes that will determine who earns a spot in the two-chef finale and who will see their dream end just short of the finish line.

programme.title: Family Guy
programme.desc: Anarchic animated sitcom about a dysfunctional family in a wacky Rhode Island town. programme.title: Family Guy
programme.desc: Anarchic animated sitcom about a dysfunctional family in a wacky Rhode Island town. programme.desc: Anarchic animated sitcom about a dysfunctional family in a wacky Rhode Island town.
